# Requirements Quality Checklist: Script Workspace

**Purpose**: Reviewer-facing requirements-quality review of the Script Workspace spec — testing whether the requirements are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable, not whether the implementation works.
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope of this checklist**: Document state integrity · LLM trust boundary · Workspace & file management · Failure & recovery UX.

## Document State Integrity

- [ ] CHK001 Is "region" in FR-015a defined precisely enough to be implemented without interpretation — i.e., does the spec state whether a region is a character range, a line range, a Markdown block, or an arbitrary quoted span? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015a]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the minimum uniqueness requirement for `anchorText` (as opposed to `expectedText`) stated in the spec, or does it exist only in the tool-call contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015a vs contracts/tool-call.md]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the behavior defined when an AI revision's target region matches the expected text but the region appears more than once in the document? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec define what "the rest of the document is unchanged" means at the character level — specifically whether whitespace, line endings, and Markdown formatting normalization outside the region are permitted to change? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the conflict-resolution requirement (FR-019) specific about *how* the user resolves a conflict — is reject, re-base, or manual-merge the expected outcome, and is any one of them mandatory? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec state a retention or pruning policy for recoverable versions (FR-020), or is "every prior version MUST be recoverable" left unbounded? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK007 Is it specified whether restoring a prior version (FR-020) itself creates a new version, so that undo is undoable? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the conditions that trigger the anti-clear guard (FR-021) quantified — what counts as "replace or clear" versus a legitimate large targeted edit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK009 Does the spec require that a revision failing to apply leaves the document byte-identical, rather than merely "unchanged" in a user-visible sense? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015b]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the relationship between autosave (FR-004) and the single write path stated — i.e., is it explicit that an AI edit and a keystroke produce the same persisted state transition? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004 vs §FR-016]

## LLM Trust Boundary

- [ ] CHK011 Does the spec state that model output must be validated before it can mutate document state, or is this guarantee present only in the plan and constitution? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK012 Is it specified what the user sees when a tool call is rejected for schema or validation failure, including whether the failed attempt is recorded in the conversation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the requirement that the style's instructions never appear in the conversation (FR-011) sufficient to also cover them appearing in an exported document, an error message, or a log? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK014 Does the spec define whether the model can be induced to clear the document by persuasion, and is the user-confirmation requirement (FR-021) framed to resist it rather than rely on model cooperation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the obligation to render Markdown safely stated in the spec at all, or does it exist only as a constitution principle? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK016 Is there a stated timeout or bounded-duration requirement for AI requests in the spec, or is "within 30 seconds" only present in a success criterion? [Consistency, Spec §SC-006 vs §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the spec define behavior when the model returns a valid-shaped revision whose `summary` is missing or misleading — is `summary` a requirement or an implementation detail? [Unspecified]
- [ ] CHK018 Is it specified whether one AI response may contain more than one document revision, and if so, how they are ordered and applied? [Edge Case, Gap]

## Workspace & File Management

- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec state which characters or lengths are permitted in a title, beyond non-blank and unique? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001b]
- [ ] CHK020 Is title uniqueness defined precisely — is it case-sensitive, whitespace-normalized, or evaluated on the trimmed value? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001b]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the behavior defined when a user attempts to rename a script to a title another script is concurrently being created with? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK022 Does the spec define what the sidebar shows for a script that has never been generated from (created, empty, no conversation content)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the ordering of the sidebar list specified (creation order, last modified, alphabetical), or left undefined? [Unspecified, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK024 Is it specified what happens to an unsaved edit when the user switches to another script (FR-003) — is the save flushed before the switch, or is the edit at risk? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK025 Does the spec state whether a script's style can be removed once assigned, or only replaced (FR-009)? [Unspecified, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the requirement that conversations are isolated (FR-006) paired with a stated consequence for how conversation state is keyed or scoped? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]

## Failure & Recovery UX

- [ ] CHK027 Is the set of save states (FR-005, "saved, pending, failed") exhaustive, or are intermediate states such as "saving, retrying, offline" left undefined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK028 Does the spec define whether a failed save is retried automatically and, if so, how many times and with what backoff? [Unspecified, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK029 Is it specified how a user recovers an edit that failed to save when they then close the browser? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK030 Are the user-facing error messages required to be distinguishable by cause (timeout, upstream error, invalid output, conflict), or could one generic message satisfy FR-022? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK031 Does the spec state whether the conversation records failed AI attempts, so that a user returning later understands why nothing changed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the requirement that the workspace must not remain in a pending state (FR-023) measurable — is a maximum pending duration stated anywhere in the requirements? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK033 Is it defined what the user sees during a long-running generation (progress indication, cancel affordance), or is only the terminal state specified? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the behavior specified when the user sends a second prompt while the first is still streaming? [Edge Case, Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK035 Is the assumption "one person, one device at a time" (Assumptions) stated strongly enough that the resulting behavior is defined — specifically, what happens if two browser tabs hold the same script? [Completeness]
- [ ] CHK036 Does the spec acknowledge that tool-calling capability varies by model, given the model is now runtime configuration, and define the user-visible consequence? [Assumption, Gap]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the 50 000-character context warning present in the requirements, or only in the plan's constraints? Does the spec say what the user is told and whether the request is blocked or attempted? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases vs plan.md]
- [ ] CHK038 Is "Deleting scripts is not addressed by this feature" (Out of Scope) consistent with the Assumption that scripts are "retained until the user removes them" — which presupposes a removal capability? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions vs §Out of Scope]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK039 Do FR-015a (region-only edits) and FR-015c (first draft is a full-document write) leave any state unaccounted for — such as a non-empty document needing a complete regeneration? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015a vs §FR-015c]
- [ ] CHK040 Is SC-002 ("90% of AI changes reach the editor without copy-paste") a meaningful success criterion, given that FR-016 makes copy-paste the forbidden path rather than an expected fraction? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK041 Is SC-005 ("zero reports of lost text") measurable within a feature scope, or does it describe an operational outcome that cannot be evaluated at acceptance time? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the term "document" used consistently with "script" throughout, or do they drift into meaning different things? [Consistency, Terminology]
- [ ] CHK043 Is "style" consistently distinguished from "skill" (the original requirement's term), and is the canonical term fixed for UI copy and code? [Consistency, Terminology]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items marked `[Gap]` reference requirements that may need to be written rather than reworded
